faq.q: What is the minimum deposit amount for FCNR?
faq.a: The minimum deposit amount for FCNR accounts varies by bank and currency. It can range from USD 1,000 to USD 5,000 equivalent, or sometimes higher for specific tenures. It's best to check with the individual bank.

faq.q: Can I prematurely withdraw my FCNR deposit?
faq.a: Yes, premature withdrawal of FCNR deposits is generally allowed. However, banks may levy a penalty for early withdrawal, typically by reducing the interest rate paid on the deposit.

FCNR deposits are bank deposits and are covered by the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) up to ₹5 lakhs per depositor per bank, in case of bank failure. [cite: RBI] However, this coverage is in Indian Rupees, so for foreign currency deposits, the actual payout would be the Rupee equivalent up to the limit.

faq.q: How is the interest paid on FCNR deposits?
faq.a: Interest on FCNR deposits is typically paid at maturity along with the principal. Some banks might offer options for periodic interest payouts (e.g., annually or semi-annually), but this is less common for FCNR accounts.

faq.q: Can resident Indians open an FCNR account?
faq.a: No, FCNR accounts are exclusively for Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs). Once an NRI returns to India and becomes a resident, the FCNR deposit must be converted into a Resident Foreign Currency (RFC) account or a resident Rupee account upon maturity or earlier.

faq.q: Is the FCNR interest rate fixed or floating?
faq.a: FCNR deposit interest rates are fixed for the entire tenure of the deposit at the time of opening the account. They do not fluctuate with market rates during the deposit period.
